title: Text someone you haven't talked to in a month. Just: “thought of you.”
why: Tiny reach-outs keep friendships alive through busy years.

title: Reply to the message you've been meaning to answer. Imperfect is fine.
why: An unanswered message quietly costs closeness. A quick reply wins it back.

title: Send a voice note instead of a text to one friend today.
why: Hearing a voice builds more closeness than reading words.

title: Ask a coworker one real question: “What's been the best part of your week?”
why: Small, sincere questions are how acquaintances start becoming friends.
evidence: Huang et al. 2017 (question asking and liking)

title: Call a family member and ask them something you've never asked before.
why: Curiosity turns a routine call into a real conversation.

title: Invite one person to a 20-minute coffee or walk this week. Name the day.
why: Friendships grow from time together, and a specific plan is far likelier to happen.

title: Tell a friend one specific thing you appreciate about them.
why: Appreciation strengthens a friendship more than most people expect.

title: Say yes to the next invitation you'd normally skip.
why: Showing up is most of friendship.

title: Host something small: three people, one easy dish or game. Send the invites today.
why: Being the one who gathers people is a skill anyone can learn.

title: Go to a class, club or meetup you've been curious about, and stay for the chat after.
why: Seeing the same faces again and again is how adult friendships form.

title: Share a song, photo or meme with someone it reminded you of.
why: “Saw this and thought of you” moments keep bonds warm with almost no effort.

title: Start a recurring thing with one friend: a weekly call or a monthly walk. Put the first one in both calendars.
why: Rituals carry friendships through the busy weeks.

title: Reply to a friend's good news with real enthusiasm and one follow-up question.
why: How you respond to good news shapes closeness, often more than how you respond to bad news.

title: Give one person a specific compliment today. Say it out loud or send it.
why: Compliments land warmer, and feel less awkward, than the giver expects.

title: Learn the name of a barista, neighbor or front-desk person you see often. Use it next time.
why: Small chats with familiar faces add real belonging to an ordinary day.

title: Ask a friend for a small recommendation you actually want: a book, a show, a lunch spot.
why: People like being asked, and they say yes far more often than we predict.

title: Send a friend a photo of a memory you share, with one line about why it still makes you smile.
why: Revisiting good times together keeps a bond warm, and it takes seconds.

title: Write the names of five people you'd like to see more of. Pick one to reach out to this week.
why: Knowing who matters to you makes the next small step obvious.

title: On your next call or coffee, ask one deeper question: “What's been on your mind lately?”
why: Deep talk feels less awkward and more rewarding than people expect, on both sides.

title: Write a short thank-you note to someone who helped you, then send it or read it to them.
why: Thanks lands far harder than the thanker expects, and lifts you both.

title: Start a friendly chat with someone new at a café, class or queue. One easy question is enough.
why: Talking to strangers is usually more pleasant than we predict, for both people.

title: Make or pick up a simple meal and share it with a roommate, neighbor or friend.
why: Sharing food is one of the oldest ways humans bond.

title: Do one small, unasked-for kindness for someone you know: a coffee, a ride, a hand with a chore.
why: Being kind to others gives the kind person a lift too.

title: Video-call a faraway friend for 20 minutes. No agenda, just catching up.
why: Distance doesn't end friendships. Going quiet does, and a call fixes that.

title: Go to week one of something weekly: a run club, choir, board-game night or volunteer crew.
why: Familiar faces, week after week, are how strangers become friends.

title: Throw a potluck: invite four people and ask each to bring one dish.
why: Shared meals turn a group of people into a group of friends.

title: Spend a few hours helping a friend with something big: a move, a project, a messy apartment.
why: Showing up for the hard stuff builds trust fast.

title: Host a game night: cards, board games or a quiz, three or more people, snacks optional.
why: Play is an easy way to rack up the hours friendships are built from.

title: Visit a friend or relative you haven't seen in person for over a year.
why: Time face to face is what turns old ties back into close ones.

title: Take a group singing or dance class, with a friend or solo, and chat with someone after.
why: Moving and singing in time with others bonds people surprisingly fast.

title: Volunteer for a few hours with a friend: a food bank, a park cleanup, an animal shelter.
why: Doing good side by side is a double win: for the cause and the friendship.

title: Host a “bring someone” hangout: each friend brings one person the others haven't met.
why: New faces widen your circle, and even light ties make days brighter.
